title: Getting around
intro: The window bar at the top, the tabs, the switch between the whole portfolio and one property, the Assistant button and making the app bigger or smaller — where everything is.

topics.title: The main screen
topics.intro: What you see when the app opens, from the top down.

steps.title: The whole window
steps.text: The app opens on the Portfolio tab. At the very top is the window bar (live rates, Settings and the window buttons). Under it: the app’s name, the property count and the version; then the tabs; then the switch between the whole portfolio and one property, the Data menu and the Needs Attention strip. The portfolio page itself starts below them.

marks.label: Window bar
marks.text: The app’s own title bar. Drag it to move the window.

marks.label: Fetch live rate
marks.text: Fetches today’s market rates and shows them in a list (next topic).

marks.label: Settings
marks.text: App size, the portfolio targets, the list of properties, this guide and the Claude connection (the Settings chapter).

marks.label: Minimize
marks.text: Hides the window to the taskbar.

marks.label: Maximize
marks.text: Fills the screen; click again to go back to the size it was.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the app.

marks.label: Living Residential
marks.text: The app’s name — nothing to click.

marks.label: Property count
marks.text: How many properties are in the portfolio. Archived properties aren’t counted. Settings lists every one by name.

marks.label: Version
marks.text: The version you have. Click it to check for a new version (the Settings chapter shows what it can say).

marks.label: Portfolio tab
marks.text: This page. It is always the first tab and can’t be closed.
Opens Underwriting, the Calendar or Data Health in a tab of its own.

marks.label: Whole Portfolio
marks.text: The whole book on one page (shown now).

marks.label: Specific Property
marks.text: One property at a time: its loans, payment schedule and profile.

marks.label: Data
marks.text: Back up, restore, and Excel export and import (the Settings, Data & backups chapter).

marks.label: Needs Attention
marks.text: Dates coming up and loans worth refinancing — click a card to go there (the Portfolio chapter).

marks.label: Portfolio
marks.text: The portfolio page: totals, charts, coverage and every loan (the Portfolio chapter).

topics.title: The window bar
topics.intro: The strip across the top of the window. It stays the same on every tab.

steps.title: Fetch live rate — the rates list
steps.text: Click Fetch live rate. The app asks the US feeds for today’s rates (the Treasury curve, SOFR and the others) and opens this list: every rate the app holds, its value, where the value comes from, and which of your loans use it. The new values are used at once by the refinance (today’s market rate), the Current / Market / Gap columns on the Portfolio page and the rate preview on the loan form. In this picture only one rate came back from the feeds; the others show the app’s built-in values. With no internet the list says so and the last saved values stay.

marks.label: Market rates
marks.text: The list of every rate the app holds.

marks.label: How many were refreshed
marks.text: How many rates came fresh from the US feeds just now, and how many rates the app holds.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the list (so does clicking outside it). The rates stay updated.

marks.label: Rate
marks.text: The rate’s name — Prime, SOFR, Term SOFR, Fed Funds, the US Treasuries and “Other”.

marks.label: Value
marks.text: The rate today, in percent.

marks.label: Where it comes from
marks.text: “live” with the date it was quoted; “Built-in rate — fetch to update” is the app’s stored value; “Last saved rate” is the last value fetched.

marks.label: Your loans on it
marks.text: Every loan of yours that uses this rate, and whether it is floating, hybrid or fixed (a fixed loan’s rate is locked and doesn’t move).

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Click Settings to open its menu. From the top: the app’s size (App scale), the portfolio targets the Portfolio page measures against, the list of every property with any possible duplicates, this guide, and the Claude connection. Each part is explained in the Settings, Data & backups chapter. Click anywhere outside the menu (or press Esc) to close it.

marks.label: Settings
marks.text: Opens and closes this menu.

marks.label: App scale
marks.text: Makes everything bigger or smaller (last topic).

marks.label: Portfolio targets
marks.text: The DSCR, LTV and debt-yield targets the Portfolio page measures against.

marks.label: Properties
marks.text: How many properties there are, every one by name, and any that look like duplicates.

marks.label: Open the guide
marks.text: Opens this guide.

marks.label: Claude connection
marks.text: Connects Claude for the AI features — your Claude subscription or an API key.

steps.title: The version and the window buttons
steps.text: On the right of the header is the version you have. Click it and the app checks for a new version; while a new version downloads it shows its progress, and once it is ready it turns green — “Update ready — Restart”: click it to restart into the new version. Your data and backups are not touched by an update. The three buttons at the top right minimize, maximize and close the window.

marks.label: Property count
marks.text: How many properties are in the portfolio (archived ones aren’t counted).

marks.label: Version
marks.text: Your version. Click to check for an update; it then reads “Checking for updates…”, “Downloading update… %”, and finally “Update ready — Restart”.

marks.label: Minimize
marks.text: Hides the window to the taskbar.

marks.label: Maximize / Restore
marks.text: Fills the screen, or puts the window back to its size.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the app.

topics.title: Tabs
topics.intro: Portfolio is always the first tab. Underwriting, the Calendar and Data Health open in tabs of their own, next to it.

steps.title: The “+” menu
steps.text: Click the “+” after the last tab. A small menu lists the tools that open in a tab. Click one: it opens as a new tab and comes to the front.

marks.label: Portfolio
marks.text: The Portfolio tab — always there, can’t be closed.
Opens this menu. Click it again to close the menu.

marks.label: Underwriting & Sizing
marks.text: A property’s T12, its NOI, loan sizing and the pro forma.

marks.label: Maturity & Reset Calendar
marks.text: Every maturity, rate reset and interest-only change, month by month.

marks.label: Data Health
marks.text: What is missing or needs a look, across every property.

steps.title: Several tabs open
steps.text: Here Underwriting, the Calendar and Data Health are all open. Click a tab to bring it to the front — each keeps its place while you look at another. Each tool opens once: choosing it again from “+” just brings its tab forward. Drag a tab left or right to change the order (Portfolio stays first).

marks.label: Portfolio
marks.text: Back to the Portfolio page.

marks.label: Underwriting
marks.text: An open tab. Click to bring it to the front.

marks.label: Calendar
marks.text: Another open tab.

marks.label: Data Health (in front)
marks.text: The tab showing now — it is white and joined to the page below.

marks.label: Pop out
marks.text: Opens this tab in a window of its own — handy on a second screen. The tab leaves the strip while its window is open (choosing the tool from “+” brings that window to the front). In the window, “Dock into main window” puts it back here as a tab, as it was; closing the window closes the tool.

marks.label: Close tab
marks.text: Closes the tab (next step).

steps.title: Close a tab
steps.text: Click the × on a tab to close it. If it was the tab in front, you land back on Portfolio. Nothing is lost — your files and figures are saved with each property; open the tool again from “+” whenever you like.

marks.label: Portfolio
marks.text: Back in front after the Data Health tab was closed.

marks.label: Underwriting
marks.text: Still open.

marks.label: Calendar
marks.text: Still open.
Opens a closed tool again.

topics.title: Whole Portfolio or one property
topics.intro: The switch under the tabs: the whole book on one page, or one property at a time.

steps.title: Whole Portfolio
steps.text: Whole Portfolio shows the whole book: Needs Attention, the totals, the charts, coverage per property, the forecast and every loan. Everything on it is explained in the Portfolio (Home) chapter.

marks.label: Whole Portfolio
marks.text: Shows the whole book (green = the one showing).

marks.label: Specific Property
marks.text: Switches to one property (next step).

marks.label: Data
marks.text: Backups and Excel — the same menu on both sides of the switch.

marks.label: Needs Attention
marks.text: Shown on the whole-portfolio side only.

steps.title: Specific Property
steps.text: Specific Property shows one property at a time: pick it in the list, and its loans, payment schedule and profile show below. The buttons beside the list add a loan or a property, edit or archive the property, and open the refinance. The property chapters explain this page. Click Whole Portfolio to go back.

marks.label: Specific Property
marks.text: One property at a time (showing now).

marks.label: Whole Portfolio
marks.text: Back to the whole book.

marks.label: Select a property
marks.text: The property to show. Pick another one here.

marks.label: Add Loan
marks.text: Adds a loan — to this property or a new one.

marks.label: Add Property
marks.text: Adds a property — a name is enough to start.

marks.label: Edit
marks.text: Edits this property’s details.

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Archives this property and its loans (they can be brought back from the Portfolio page).

marks.label: Refi Calculator
marks.text: Opens the refinance for this property.

topics.title: The Assistant button
topics.intro: The green button at the bottom right, on every tab.

steps.title: Ask the assistant
steps.text: The Assistant button sits at the bottom right of the window on every tab. Click it to ask Claude about your portfolio, or to ask it to do something in the app for you. The Assistant chapter shows it in full. Claude must be connected for it to answer (Settings → Claude connection).

marks.label: Assistant
marks.text: Opens the assistant window.

topics.title: Make everything bigger or smaller
topics.intro: App scale in Settings zooms the whole app, like zoom in a web browser.

steps.title: App scale
steps.text: Open Settings. Drag the App scale slider, or click one of the sizes under it: the whole app grows or shrinks at once, like zoom in a web browser — at 75% more of the page fits on the screen, at 150% everything is easier to read. The window bar at the top always stays the same size, so Settings is always easy to reach. Reset to 100% puts it back; the app also goes back to 100% each time you open it.

marks.label: Settings
marks.text: Opens this menu. The window bar it sits in never zooms.

marks.label: Size now
marks.text: The size the app is at.

marks.label: Slider
marks.text: Drag it: 50% (small) to 200% (big), in steps of 5%.

marks.label: Reset to 100%
marks.text: Back to the normal size.
